gloss: sukiyaki pot; shallow iron pot for sukiyaki

definitions.gloss: sukiyaki pot; shallow iron pot for sukiyaki
definitions.explanation: A wide, shallow, heavy iron or cast-iron pot specifically designed for cooking sukiyaki. Its flat bottom and low sides allow ingredients to be simmered in a thin layer of sweet soy-based broth at the table.

examples.japanese: すき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ}を{火|ひ}にかけた。
examples.english: I put the sukiyaki pot on the heat.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}から{鉄|てつ}のすき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ}を{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ。
examples.english: I inherited an iron sukiyaki pot from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}にはいつも{家族|かぞく}で{大|おお}きなすき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ}を{囲|かこ}んで{食事|しょくじ}をする。
examples.english: At New Year's, our family always gathers around a large sukiyaki pot for a meal.

notes:
Composed of すき{焼|や}き (sukiyaki, a Japanese hot pot dish) and {鍋|なべ} (pot). The traditional すき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ} is made of cast iron ({鋳鉄|ちゅうてつ}) and has a wide, flat shape that distinguishes it from deeper hot pot vessels.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- すき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ}を{囲|かこ}む: to gather around a sukiyaki pot
- {鉄|てつ}のすき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ}: iron sukiyaki pot
- すき{焼|や}き{鍋|なべ}に{具材|ぐざい}を{入|い}れる: to add ingredients to the sukiyaki pot

CULTURAL NOTE:
Sukiyaki is traditionally cooked at the table, so the pot is both a cooking vessel and a serving dish. In many families, a well-seasoned cast-iron sukiyaki pot is a treasured kitchen heirloom passed down through generations.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {土鍋|どなべ}: clay pot — used for nabemono (Japanese hot pot), deeper than a sukiyaki pot
- {鉄鍋|てつなべ}: iron pot — general term; the sukiyaki pot is a specific type
- フライパン: frying pan — similar shape but different material and purpose
